annotation.title_clean: An Act Relating to Motor Vehicles; Adding Definitions to the Motor Vehicle Code; Providing for Autonomous Motor Vehicles; Requiring Permits; Allowing Platooning of Motor Vehicles (HB 270)
annotation.title_en: An Act Relating to Motor Vehicles; Adding Definitions to the Motor Vehicle Code; Providing for Autonomous Motor Vehicles; Requiring Permits; Allowing Platooning of Motor Vehicles (HB 270)
annotation.summary_en: New Mexico House Bill 270 amends the Motor Vehicle Code to define automated driving systems (SAE levels 3-5), autonomous vehicles and platooning. It requires five-day advance notice to the Department of Transportation before public-road testing, mandates FMVSS compliance, bars local bans, and assigns accident notification duties to owners. Effective July 1, 2022.
key_provisions_or_claims: Defines automated driving system by reference to SAE J3016 levels 3-5, plus autonomous vehicle, operator and operational design domain.
Requires notice to the Department of Transportation at least five days before public-highway testing, with vehicle serial number, routes and automation level.
Autonomous vehicles must meet federal motor vehicle safety standards and be capable of complying with New Mexico traffic law.
Political subdivisions may not prohibit autonomous vehicle testing or operation solely because of the automated driving system.
Owner must give accident notice for driverless vehicles; driver-assisted platooning is exempt from following-distance rules.
